title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: The numbers here represent the hh reached by Nafa Quick + 16,966 hh reached by the regular Nafa Program, using the average rural household size of 10.9. The target of 654,000 was exceeded. The Nafa Quick is complete and will be replaced by the regular Naf Program which targets a sub-set of these beneficiaries, i.e. just the extreme poor.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs
Number of households identified as extremely poor included in the Nafa program

comment.narrative: The number of extremely poor households in the Nafa project represents the total number of extreme poor expected to be found in the selected districts that will be identified through the PMT and community validation. 'In' the program means that they are registered and have received at least the Introductory SBCC module about the program.  The Nafa Program launched in late September 2021 in three districts, and scaled up in July 2022 to 17 additional districts.

title.narrative: Number of households identified as extremely poor included in the Nafa program
Number of programs using the Social Registry

comment.narrative: This indicator measures how many programs will have used the Social Registry data to identify eligible beneficiaries, to avoid duplications, or create synergies between programs. MoUs have been signed with and data has been transferred and used by Nafa Program, ROOTS Project, NDMA, 2 agencies working with the MoA for the China Rice Aid Distribution, and WFP for the 2023 lean season response.
